rows.description: I look down on classmates who are poorer or on scholarships. Wise: notice how privilege shapes me and treat people by who they are.

rows.description: I am ashamed of my parents' job or our home when friends visit. Wise: the shame is learned; dignity of work is real, and true friends care about me, not the house.

rows.description: I overhear my parents fight about debts and fees. I feel scared and guilty for costing money. Wise: ask what is happening, offer help within my role, and remember I am a child, not the fixer.

rows.description: My parent hides the money problem to protect me. I sense it anyway. Wise: say kindly that I can handle honesty, and adjust my asks without blaming them.

rows.description: Friends have new phones and trips while I can't. I feel bitter. Wise: acknowledge the feeling, focus on what I have, and avoid pretending or borrowing to keep up.

rows.description: I consider working part-time or dropping studies to help. Wise: discuss with family and a teacher; look for scholarships and small safe earning, keeping education first.
